name: PCA territory, temporal
synonyms: anterior and posterior temporal artery territory
summary: The temporal PCA territory is the inferomedial temporal lobe supplied by the anterior and posterior temporal branches of the posterior cerebral artery's P2 segment: the parahippocampal, fusiform and inferior temporal gyri, the hippocampus (with the anterior choroidal artery) and the temporal pole's inferior surface. It is the territory of the memory and recognition syndromes of PCA stroke: amnesia, prosopagnosia and visual agnosia, and it contributes the upper quadrant defect through Meyer's loop. It borders the MCA temporal territory along the inferior temporal gyrus, a watershed, and it is the cortex compressed against the tentorium and infarcted by PCA compression during uncal herniation.

anatomy.location: Inferomedial temporal lobe from the temporal pole to the occipito-temporal junction, including the parahippocampal gyrus, the hippocampus, the fusiform gyrus and the inferior temporal gyrus, resting on the tentorium and the middle cranial fossa floor; bounded laterally by the MCA temporal territory, medially by the anterior choroidal territory of the hippocampal head and posteriorly by the occipital PCA territory.

afferents.from: Anterior and posterior temporal branches of the P2 segment

efferents.to: Basal vein of Rosenthal and inferior temporal veins

function: The territory contains the medial temporal memory system (hippocampus, entorhinal and parahippocampal cortex) and the ventral visual recognition cortex (fusiform face and word areas, inferior temporal object areas), so its infarction produces amnesia, which is severe and permanent when bilateral, prosopagnosia and landmark agnosia on the right, and associative agnosia and alexia on the left, together with the upper quadrant defect from the temporal optic radiation. The P2 segment runs in the ambient cistern beside the uncus and is compressed in uncal herniation, producing a secondary PCA infarct of this territory.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion of the parahippocampal and fusiform gyri and the hippocampus with amnesia, agnosia and an upper quadrantanopia.

pathology.pathology: Secondary PCA infarct in uncal herniation
pathology.finding: Hypodensity of the medial temporal and occipital lobes days after a supratentorial mass compressed the P2 segment against the tentorium.
Punctate hippocampal diffusion lesions at 24-72 hours with no territorial infarct.
